name: Napa Valley
blurb: California’s most famous fine-wine valley; Cabernet Sauvignon is king on valley floor and foothills, with Chardonnay and Merlot also important. Double-click for sub-AVAs and a winery timeline PoC.

name: Sonoma County
blurb: Diverse AVAs from foggy Russian River Pinot/Chardonnay to warmer Alexander and Dry Creek Valley Cabernet and Zinfandel. Double-click for sub-AVAs and wineries.

name: Central Coast
blurb: Broad coastal corridor from SF Bay to Santa Barbara; cool Pacific influence inland to warmer pockets. Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Cabernet, and Rhône varieties.

name: Paso Robles
blurb: Warm inland Central Coast AVA; day–night swings suit Cabernet, Rhône blends, and Zinfandel. Growing prestige for Syrah and GSM-style wines.

name: Santa Barbara
blurb: East–west valleys (Santa Ynez, Sta. Rita Hills) channel cool ocean air; Pinot Noir and Chardonnay are classics, with Rhône varieties inland.

name: Mendocino
blurb: North of Sonoma; Anderson Valley is cool (Pinot, sparkling), while inland Ukiah/Redwood Valley are warmer (Zinfandel, Cabernet).

name: Sierra Foothills
blurb: Gold Country elevations; old-vine Zinfandel heritage plus Barbera, Syrah, and Rhône whites. Climate point: Placerville (El Dorado).

name: Lodi
blurb: Inland Sacramento–San Joaquin Delta influence; major source of Zinfandel (including old vines) and everyday Cabernet/Chardonnay.

name: Monterey
blurb: Long Salinas Valley with strong afternoon winds; Chardonnay and Pinot Noir in cooler zones, Merlot/Cabernet farther south/inland.
